data.statement: Move per-user writable application data (settings.json and the Logs directory) out of the application root into a per-user OS data location (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support on macOS) with an AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override, keep the app-root settings.json as a read-only bundled default that seeds the per-user file on first run, and make initialize_logging degrade to console-only instead of raising so a read-only install directory (Program Files or a system-wide Linux install) can no longer crash startup before any log exists.

acceptance: config exposes a per-user writable data root that resolves to %LOCALAPPDATA%/AudioMancer on Windows, XDG_DATA_HOME/AudioMancer or ~/.local/share/AudioMancer on Linux, and ~/Library/Application Support/AudioMancer on macOS.
Setting AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR overrides the resolved per-user data root on every platform, so portable and CI runs can pin the location.
config.APP_SETTINGS_PATH resolves under the per-user data root and no longer under config.APP_ROOT.
The application log directory resolves under the per-user data root and no longer under config.APP_ROOT.
A read-only application root no longer prevents startup: with APP_ROOT non-writable and a writable per-user data root, settings load and save plus logging initialization all succeed.
initialize_logging() does not raise when the log directory cannot be created or the log file cannot be opened; it installs a console-only root logger and reports that no log file was created.
app.main() completes its bootstrap normally when logging initialization produced no log file.

On first run with no per-user settings file, settings are seeded from the bundled default settings file at APP_ROOT/settings.json when that file is readable, and from build_default_settings() otherwise; the seeded payload is written to the per-user location and the bundled file is never written to.
config exposes the bundled default settings path separately from the per-user settings path, and the committed scaffold contract tests assert against the bundled path.
The frozen-bundle resource contract still resolves prompts, help, licences and version from the bundle root, and settings.json still counts as a runtime-resource marker.
The configured test and lint gates pass, and audit traceability and audit coverage report no blocking findings.
assumptions: A pure-stdlib platform resolver is preferred over QStandardPaths: config.py is imported by every module including headless tests and must not pull in PySide6, and QStandardPaths.AppDataLocation appends QCoreApplication applicationName, which is still empty when config is imported at startup, so it would resolve a wrong path at exactly the moment the path is needed.

The app-root settings.json stays committed and packaged as the read-only default scaffold; it keeps working as a runtime-root marker in _has_runtime_resource_markers() and becomes the seed for the per-user file, so existing source-tree and portable users keep their current settings on first run after the change.

Per-user relocation is unconditional rather than per-user-only-when-APP_ROOT-is-not-writable, because a writability probe is racy, differs between elevated and normal runs, and would leave two possible settings locations for the same install.

Windows and Linux behaviour is verified by monkeypatched platform and environment tests on the local Windows host; no Linux runner is available in this environment, so cross-platform proof is test-level rather than execution-level.
open_questions: Approve proceeding at risk level medium? The change relocates where operator settings and application logs live, and edits the startup path that every run goes through.
Confirm the resolver is pure stdlib (platform plus environment variables) rather than PySide6 QStandardPaths, even though the ticket names QStandardPaths?
Confirm unconditional per-user relocation with an AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR escape hatch, rather than a portable mode that keeps data in APP_ROOT when APP_ROOT is writable?
data.reason: Workflow policy sets alignment.risk_threshold = medium with pause_on_open_questions = true, and this change both carries medium risk (operator data location plus the startup path) and raises three design questions. Recommended responses are recorded so the human can approve in one step.
recommended_responses: Approve. The relocation is additive at the filesystem level: the bundled settings.json seeds the per-user copy on first run, so an existing source-tree or portable user sees identical settings, and the logging change strictly removes a startup failure mode rather than adding one.

Yes, pure stdlib. It satisfies the intent of the ticket (per-user OS data location: %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, XDG on Linux) while keeping config.py free of a Qt import, and it avoids QStandardPaths.AppDataLocation resolving against an empty applicationName during bootstrap.

Yes, unconditional with the AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override. One deterministic location per install avoids a writability probe whose result changes between elevated and normal runs, and the environment override covers the portable-zip and CI cases explicitly.
scope: IN: a per-user writable data root resolver in config.py (Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share, macOS ~/Library/Application Support) with an AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override; new config constants for the user data root, the per-user settings path, and the bundled default settings path; APP_SETTINGS_PATH repointed to the per-user location; logging_service log directory repointed to the per-user location; initialize_logging() degraded to console-only on OSError instead of raising; settings_service first-run seeding from the bundled default settings file; app.py bootstrap made resilient to a logging init that produced no file; new and updated tests; component documentation; requirement snapshots. OUT: moving read-only packaged resources (prompts, help, LICENSE, icon, pyproject) off APP_ROOT; any change to settings schema, defaults, validation rules or the settings UI; project-workspace paths and per-project artifacts, which are already operator-chosen; the APP_ROOT default directory used by the project open/create file dialogs; log format, retention or level policy; adding PySide6 QStandardPaths as a config.py dependency; packaging and installer changes.

data.understanding: config.APP_SETTINGS_PATH (config.py:180) and logging_service._log_directory_path() (logging_service.py:176) both derive writable runtime data from config.APP_ROOT, which resolve_app_runtime_root() sets to the source-tree root, the installed wheel resource root, or the PyInstaller bundle root. For a frozen build installed into a non-writable location (Program Files on Windows, a system-wide prefix on Linux), settings.json cannot be written and Logs/ cannot be created. initialize_logging() calls log_directory.mkdir(parents=True) and then logging.FileHandler(...), and app.py:50 calls it before the try/except, so an OSError there aborts startup with a raw traceback and no log file at all. The fix separates two concerns: (1) writable per-user data moves to an OS-standard per-user location, keeping the app-root settings.json as a read-only bundled default that seeds the per-user copy on first run, which also migrates existing portable and source installs for free; (2) initialize_logging() becomes non-fatal, degrading to a console-only root logger when the log directory or file cannot be opened, so an unusable data location can never crash the bootstrap before logging exists. Read-only packaged resources (prompts, help, LICENSE, icon, pyproject) stay under APP_ROOT and are unchanged.

acceptance: config exposes a resolved writable data root and the resolver honours AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR ahead of every other candidate on every platform.

With no override and a writable application root, the resolved data root is the application root, so APP_SETTINGS_PATH and the log directory keep their current locations for source-tree and portable runs.

With no override and a non-writable application root, the resolved data root is %LOCALAPPDATA%/AudioMancer on Windows, XDG_DATA_HOME/AudioMancer or ~/.local/share/AudioMancer on Linux, and ~/Library/Application Support/AudioMancer on macOS.
A writable PyInstaller _MEIPASS extraction directory is never selected as the data root; the per-user location is used instead.
config.APP_SETTINGS_PATH and the application log directory both derive from the resolved data root rather than directly from config.APP_ROOT.
A read-only application root no longer prevents startup: settings load and save plus logging initialization all succeed against the per-user fallback location.
initialize_logging() does not raise when the log directory cannot be created or the log file cannot be opened; it installs a console-only root logger, records that logging degraded, and returns None.
app.main() completes its bootstrap normally when logging initialization produced no log file.

On first run with no settings file at an active settings path that differs from the bundled default path, settings are seeded from the bundled default file when it is readable and valid, and from build_default_settings() otherwise; the bundled file is never written to.
config exposes the bundled default settings path separately from the active settings path.
The frozen-bundle resource contract still resolves prompts, help, licences and version from the bundle root, and settings.json still counts as a runtime-resource marker.
The configured test and lint gates pass, and audit traceability and audit coverage report no blocking findings.
assumptions: Human decision: the resolver is pure stdlib rather than QStandardPaths, because config.py is imported by every module including headless tests and must not pull in PySide6, and QStandardPaths.AppDataLocation appends QCoreApplication applicationName, which is still empty when config is imported during bootstrap.

Human decision: relocation is conditional. A writable application root keeps settings and logs in place, so source-tree, portable-zip and developer runs behave identically to today and the existing contract tests keep asserting the same paths. Only a genuinely non-writable install root falls back to the OS per-user location.

Writability is proven by an actual probe file created and removed under the application root, not by os.access, because on Windows os.access(path, os.W_OK) ignores directory ACLs and reports Program Files as writable.

The PyInstaller _MEIPASS extraction directory must be excluded from the portable branch even though it is writable, otherwise a onefile build would persist settings into a temporary folder that the bootloader deletes on exit.

The app-root settings.json stays committed and packaged as the read-only default scaffold; it keeps working as a runtime-root marker in _has_runtime_resource_markers() and seeds the per-user file when the two paths differ, so an existing installation keeps its settings on first run after the change.

Windows and Linux fallback behaviour is verified by monkeypatched platform and environment tests on the local Windows host; no Linux runner is available in this environment, so cross-platform proof is test-level rather than execution-level.

data.understanding: config.APP_SETTINGS_PATH (config.py:180) and logging_service._log_directory_path() (logging_service.py:176) both derive writable runtime data from config.APP_ROOT, which resolve_app_runtime_root() sets to the source-tree root, the installed wheel resource root, or the PyInstaller bundle root. First, a new writable-data-root resolver decides once, at import time, where per-user data lives: an explicit AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override wins; otherwise the application root is used when it actually accepts writes (preserving portable and source-tree behaviour exactly as today); otherwise the OS per-user data location is used (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support on macOS). settings.json and the Logs directory both move to that resolved root, and the app-root settings.json becomes the read-only bundled default that seeds the per-user copy on first run. Second, initialize_logging() becomes non-fatal, degrading to a console-only root logger and returning None when the log directory or log file cannot be opened, so an unusable data location can never crash the bootstrap before logging exists. data.rationale: A frozen build installed into Program Files or a system-wide Linux prefix cannot write under the application root, so writable data needs a resolved location that stays next to the application whenever that is actually possible.
data.requirement: The application shall resolve one writable data root by taking the AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override first, then the application root when a probe file proves it accepts writes and it is not the PyInstaller extraction directory, and otherwise the per-user OS data location for the running platform.
data.verification: Automated: 10 linked pytest selectors covering the override, blank-override skip, writable portable root, non-directory root, Windows LOCALAPPDATA and APPDATA fallbacks, Linux XDG_DATA_HOME and ~/.local/share fallbacks, macOS Application Support, and _MEIPASS rejection.

data.rationale: Deriving writable runtime data from the packaged-resource root is what made a read-only installation directory fatal.
data.requirement: The active settings file path and the application log directory shall both derive from the resolved writable data root rather than directly from the application root.
data.verification: Automated: 4 linked pytest selectors asserting APP_SETTINGS_PATH and the log directory follow the resolved data root for the override, read-only-install and frozen-bundle layouts.

data.rationale: Seeding from the packaged settings.json migrates an existing installation to the per-user location without the operator losing configuration, while keeping the packaged copy read-only.
data.requirement: When the active settings file is missing and its path differs from the bundled default settings path, the application shall seed it from the validated bundled default payload when that file is readable and holds a JSON object, and from the built-in defaults otherwise, without ever writing to the bundled file.
data.verification: Automated: 5 linked pytest selectors covering seeding from a valid packaged scaffold, fallback on a malformed scaffold, the coinciding-path portable case, the absent-scaffold case, and the packaged file staying byte-identical.

data.rationale: initialize_logging runs before the bootstrap try/except, so any filesystem error there crashed the application with no log to diagnose it from.
data.requirement: Logging initialization shall never abort application startup: when the log directory cannot be created or the log file cannot be opened it shall install a console-only root logger, record one degraded-logging warning, and return no log file path, and log retention cleanup shall not propagate filesystem errors.
data.verification: Automated: 4 linked pytest selectors covering mkdir failure, log-file open failure, unremovable expired retention entries, and a bootstrap that received no log file path.
